NEW DELHI: IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar, called the ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, has become the first woman officer to lead CRPF ’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA.Parashar, a 2006-batch officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, earned the moniker of Iron Lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit National Democratic Front of Bodoland in 2013-14 as the then Sonitpur SP.Parashar, who is from Assam, has served both in her cadre as well as in NIA, specialising in key counter-terror investigations. She was heading the CID wing of Assam Police before being appointed IG, CoBRA.She will head CoBRA at a time when the force is engaged in holding and securing large forest areas, mostly in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, reclaimed from Naxals. These operations played a key role in almost eliminating Left-wing extremism in the country by March 2026.Two battalions of the force are also posted in Manipur, which has been witnessing intermittent violence fuelled by ethnic tensions.Parashar’s appointment as IG, CoBRA is part of a larger push by CRPF to place its women officers in lead roles, including ones that are operations- and combat-heavy.“Women are heading sectors like Jammu, CoBRA, Rapid Action Force, North East, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh as IG,” a CRPF officer told TOI.A few days ago, A Vijaya Laxmi, a 2006-batch IPS officer, was posted as IG, Jammu, a sensitive sector. Nitu D Bhattacharya heads MP sector as IG and oversaw the end of Naxalism in Balaghat. Kavita Jalan, an Odisha cadre IPS officer, is heading the North East sector that includes the whole of Meghalaya and parts of Assam. Archana Shivhare, a Gujarat cadre IPS officer, is IG, Rajasthan.RAF is also led by officer Seema Dhundia, inducted in the CRPF in 1987 as part of the first batch of female officers.Parashar had, at the start of her career as an assistant commandant, handled clashes between Bodos and illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. As Sonitpur SP, she led a crackdown on NDFB, leading to the killing of 16 militants and the arrest of 64 others. Her picture leading an operation with an AK-47 in her hand earned her the title ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, as well as death threats from Bodo militants.
Article Summary: IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar has become the first woman officer to lead CRPF’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA. She earned the moniker of Iron Lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit National Democratic Front of Bodoland in 2013-14 as the then Sonitpur SP.

Article Title: From jewellery to robots, 70-member Team India set for WorldSkills
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An eighth-pass jewellery trainee, a Class XI florist, a farmer’s son trained in refrigeration and young specialists in robotics, cyber security and Industry 4.0 will form India’s unusually diverse challenge at the “Olympics of Skills” in Shanghai this month.India will field 70 competitors across 63 skill categories at WorldSkills 2026, scheduled from September 22 to 27. The contingent spans 16 states and brings together students, apprentices and young professionals trained in traditional trades as well as emerging technologies. The line-up, however, remains heavily male-dominated: only 14 of the 70 competitors are women.Karnataka has the largest representation with 16 contestants, followed by Odisha with 13 and Tamil Nadu with 12. Maharashtra has five competitors, while Bihar, Haryana, Telangana and Gujarat have three each.Among those heading to Shanghai is Md Dilkhush of Bihar, whose father is a farmer. Trained in refrigeration and air conditioning, Dilkhush emerged as the IndiaSkills national champion and will be tested on installation, maintenance, fault diagnosis and energy-efficient cooling systems.Tamil Nadu’s Joy Das, son of a fisherman, studied till Class VIII and trained in jewellery-making before winning gold at the state and national levels.Mizoram’s Lawmnakima, a Class XI student, will compete in floristry, while Gujarat’s Prakash Suthar has followed his carpenter father into joinery.The contingent also reflects how vocational pathways are increasingly cutting across family and educational backgrounds. Anuja Vare of Karnataka, whose parents are doctors, will compete in visual merchandising. She has previously designed an exhibition space at Bharat Tex that was visited by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and won gold at the regional and national skill competitions.Telangana’s Mehrunissa Begum moved from an apprenticeship in logistics and freight forwarding to successive gold medals at the state, regional and national levels. The daughter of a bakery owner and a homemaker, she has spoken of overcoming anxiety and the feeling of being overwhelmed during her competition journey.Smriti Nambiar of Karnataka, a bakery competitor trained at IHM Pusa, was named the institute’s All-Rounder Student and Rising Culinarian for two consecutive years. Odisha’s Krishnanjali Sahoo will represent the country in patisserie and confectionery, while Jhansirani Rout will compete in restaurant service.The team also carries a strong green-skills component. Rajasthan’s Vishnu Prajapat, whose father is an electrician, will compete in renewable energy after gaining hands-on experience in solar installations and exposure to wind turbines. Rushikesh Pithambaram will represent India in water technology.At the technology end of the spectrum, the Indian contingent will compete in autonomous mobile robotics, cloud computing, cyber security, software testing, unmanned aerial systems, optoelectronics and robot systems integration. Mobile-app developer Arjun Vijayabashkar began coding at 12, while Industry 4.0 contestant Suhan Mascarenhas is the son of two employees of Isro’s Master Control Facility in Hassan.Maharashtra’s Harsh Pawar, whose father works as a quality supervisor at a cylinder-manufacturing company, will compete in 3D digital game art. Pawar has already won silver at the Global Skills Challenge in Australia. Two-member teams will represent India in areas such as autonomous mobile robotics, mechatronics, landscape gardening, concrete construction and robot systems integration.The 48th edition will open on September 22, with competitions running from September 23 to 26 and the closing ceremony on September 27. Participants will perform industry-standard assignments under the scrutiny of international experts. The event will also host a conference and industry exhibitions on technical education, workforce development and sustainable technologies.India will seek to improve on its WorldSkills Lyon 2024 performance, where it secured four bronze medals and 12 Medallions of Excellence.
Article Summary: India will field 70 competitors across 63 skill categories at WorldSkills 2026. The contingent spans 16 states and brings together students, apprentices and young professionals trained in traditional trades as well as emerging technologies. The line-up, however, remains heavily male-dominated: only 14 of the 70 competitors are women.

NEW DELHI: Israel on Monday wished India a happy Hindi Diwas , calling Hindi an "ancient language" that is "still very much alive today"."Two ancient languages, still very much alive today. Israel would like to wish everyone हिंदी दिवस की हार्दिक शुभकमनाएं!," Reuven Azar, Israel's ambassador to India, wrote on X.Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday extended heartfelt greetings to citizens on the occasion of Hindi Diwas, highlighting the role of the language in public communication, good governance and national integration, while calling for the empowerment of all Indian languages.In a post on X, HM Shah said, “Heartfelt greetings to all fellow citizens on Hindi Diwas. As the official language, Hindi is playing a vital role in strengthening public communication, good governance, and national integration.”“Hindi, which moves forward alongside all Indian languages, is now also becoming the language of technology and research. On the occasion of Official Language Day, I pay my respects to all the great personalities who have made an unforgettable contribution to enriching Hindi. Let us, on this occasion, resolve to empower all Indian languages, including Hindi,” he added.Defence minister Rajnath Singh also extended his greetings, describing Hindi as an important expression of India’s culture, civilisation and values.Singh posted on X, “Hindi is not merely a language, but a powerful expression of India’s culture, civilization, and life values. It is the language that weaves our diversity into the thread of unity. Enhancing the glory of Hindi is an act of honoring our rich linguistic and cultural heritage. Let us resolve to preserve, promote, and propagate Hindi, and make it even more robust in the fields of knowledge, science, technology, and innovation.Heartfelt greetings to all Hindi enthusiasts on Hindi Diwas.”Hindi Diwas is observed every year on September 14 to commemorate the adoption of Hindi in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on September 14, 1949. The observance of Hindi Diwas began on September 14, 1953, and has continued since then.

Konchar bolsters Knicks depth alongside Drummond

John Konchar has agreed to a one-year deal with the New York Knicks, according to ESPN's Shams Charania, giving the defending champions a fresh body on the wing just as free agency winds down. The move fills a real need for a team built to defend its crown around Jalen Brunson.Konchar arrives after a chaotic stretch that saw him moved twice in a matter of weeks. He is one of the more seasoned role players still floating around the market, and New York had to beat out a handful of suitors to get a deal done.John Konchar entered unrestricted free agency this offseason after a strange run through the trade market. Utah shipped him and Cody Williams to Minnesota for Josh Green and cash, only for the Timberwolves to waive him almost immediately. The Knicks scooped him up from there.Last season, split between Memphis and Utah, Konchar played 56 games and put up 4.4 points, 4.3 rebounds and 2.1 assists in just under 20 minutes a night. He has spent most of his career with the Grizzlies since entering the league undrafted back in 2019.Getting this deal done was not simple. The Knicks had company from the Heat, the Magic and the Raptors, all Eastern Conference teams that could have used a player like this.Konchar picked New York anyway, choosing a shot at a repeat title over a bigger role elsewhere.For a team chasing back-to-back championships, adding a defensive-minded wing on a short, cheap contract is low risk. The 6-foot-5 forward will not headline anything, but that has never really been his job.Konchar now slots in next to Andre Drummond as one of New York's more notable offseason pickups, even if neither move grabbed headlines. The Knicks still have two open roster spots, and word is there will be a real training camp battle for one of them, with the 15th spot possibly left open entirely.He brings plenty of mileage to the locker room too, with more than 360 NBA games under his belt. Over his career, he has bounced between a steady bench role in Memphis and a brief, unspectacular stint in Utah, where he averaged 5.9 points, 3.0 assists and 5.7 rebounds in 26 games last season.

Article Title: The curious case of Kelsey Plum: WNBA star who gave up $1.4M deal and asked for exactly $999,999— nobody knows why it’s one dollar short of $1m
Article Text:
Kelsey Plum. Image via: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images

Kelsey Plum deliberately stopped at $999,999

Plum eventually explained the missing dollar

The $13,000 tax saving did not work quite like that

marginal

$13,000 saving

Plum gave up much more than one dollar

FILE - Los Angeles Sparks guard Kelsey Plum dribbles during the second half of a WNBA basketball game against the Indiana Fever, May 13, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong, File)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There was nothing particularly unusual about Kelsey Plum agreeing to stay in Los Angeles for another season. The strange part was the number attached to the deal. When the details emerged, the Sparks guard had agreed to a salary of exactly $999,999, leaving one very conspicuous dollar missing from what could have been a much cleaner $1 million.Plum agreed to a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Sparks on April 12, 2026, shortly after a strong first season in Los Angeles had put her in position for a substantial new deal.The 31-year-old had arrived with the Sparks after the major three-team trade involving the Las Vegas Aces, Seattle Storm and Los Angeles, in which Plum went to Los Angeles, Jewell Loyd moved to Las Vegas and Seattle acquired the rights to the No. 2 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, which became Dominique Malonga, along with additional draft picks changing hands.Plum settled in quickly, she averaged 19.5 points per game during her first season with the Sparks and helped the team enjoy its best campaign since 2020. With the new WNBA Collective Bargaining Agreement subsequently raising salaries across the league, Plum had been eligible for a veteran supermax worth as much as $1.4 million.Instead, she signed for exactly $999,999.The difference between the figure on the contract and the round number was only $1, but Plum had actually agreed to leave roughly $400,000 of potential salary on the table.Plum wanted to give Los Angeles additional room under the salary cap to build a stronger team around her, with the aim of turning the Sparks into a genuine championship contender.At the time, however, the missing dollar was what caught everybody's attention.The mystery lasted only a few weeks before Plum was asked about it directly.In an interview with YouTuber Austin Franklin, Plum explained why she had stopped at $999,999 rather than accepting an even $1 million.Her first answer was straightforward.“I mean, first of all, taxes,” Plum said.“If you claim a million dollars, I saved $13,000 [in taxes] in not claiming a dollar.”Plum then explained that the decision had taken on a life of its own after the contract became public.“It's funny, everywhere I go now, people are like, 'Hey, can I give you a dollar?'” Plum said. “I think it's great. They're tuned in, you know?”She then offered another reason for deliberately staying below the seven-figure mark.“And the other thing was just like, I didn't want validation for signing for a million. It was like, I don't need to sign for a million to know my value as a player. It was a combination of that, but really more the taxes.”That explanation made the $999,999 figure considerably more interesting, because Plum was not simply trying to create a funny contract number. She said she had made a conscious decision to avoid crossing the $1 million threshold.There was just one problem with the way she described the tax saving.The tax explanation quickly attracted attention from people who pointed out that California's so-called “millionaire's tax” does not work by suddenly taxing an entire salary at 13 per cent once a player reaches $1 million.California currently has the highest top marginal income tax rate in the United States, reaching 13.3 per cent on income above $1 million. The important word is: the higher rate applies to the income above the relevant threshold rather than retroactively applying to every dollar earned.Entrepreneur and sports-business content creator Joe Pompliano was among those to challenge Plum's calculation.“Someone please explain marginal tax rates to Kelsey Plum. If she earned one more dollar, she would be taxed 13 cents…not $13,000. And even if that were true, she is ignoring jock taxes, endorsement income, etc,” Pompliano wrote.In other words, moving from $999,999 to $1 million would not, by itself, create a $13,000 California tax bill. On the simplified example, the additional dollar reaching the threshold would generate roughly 13 cents of tax at a 13 per cent marginal rate, rather than suddenly exposing the entire $1 million to that rate.The situation can become more complicated for professional athletes because their overall taxable income can include money from endorsements and income earned in different jurisdictions, but the basic marginal-tax principle remains the same.So while Plum's decision to stay one dollar below $1 million was real, the specificshe cited was not supported by the marginal-rate calculation described by tax commentators.The tax debate made the $999,999 figure even more memorable, but the bigger financial decision was hiding in plain sight.Plum was eligible for a $1.4 million veteran supermax, meaning she could have earned substantially more than the amount written into her contract.Instead, she accepted $999,999 and gave the Sparks more flexibility to improve the roster.That sacrifice fitted with what Plum said about not needing a seven-figure salary to validate her worth as a player. The decision was also tied to the larger ambition she had for Los Angeles after helping the Sparks produce their best season in several years.Whether the Sparks ultimately built the championship-level roster Plum had hoped for became a separate question during the 2026 season.The curious contract, meanwhile, did not last quite as long as Plum might have expected.In August 2026, just months after signing the deal, Plum was traded to the Phoenix Mercury.The $999,999 contract had therefore already become more than a quirky number. It was a snapshot of a moment when Plum wanted to stay in Los Angeles, believed in what the Sparks could build and was willing to take less money to help make it happen.And, for reasons that will probably keep the dollar joke alive for a while, she made sure the number stopped at $999,999 rather than $1 million.
Article Summary: Kelsey Plum agreed to a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Sparks on April 12, 2026, shortly after a strong first season in Los Angeles. The strange part was the number attached to the deal: $999,999. Plum eventually explained the missing dollar. She said she had made a conscious decision to avoid crossing the $1 million threshold. California currently has the highest income tax rate in the United States.

Kevin Durant has made a fortune from basketball, but one of his more intriguing financial moves came well away from the court. Long before artificial intelligence became one of the biggest investment stories in the world. The Houston Rockets star was putting money into a young technology company years before it became a major player in the open-source AI world. Years later, that decision has put a surprisingly large figure next to what was originally a relatively modest bet.The investment began when Hugging Face was still a relatively young technology company, long before artificial intelligence became such a dominant part of the technology industry. Durant and his longtime business partner Rich Kleiman backed the company through their investment platform, 35V, taking part in two of its early fundraising rounds.According to entrepreneur and sports-business writer Joe Pompliano, Durant invested $100,000 during Hugging Face's seed round before committing another $150,000 in its Series A financing. Together, those investments amounted to $250,000.That was a small commitment compared with the scale of Durant's basketball earnings, but it was made at a particularly early stage of Hugging Face's development.The company would go on to become one of the most widely used platforms for sharing and working with open-source AI models, building a large community around the development and distribution of AI technology.Durant was not hiding his involvement. In 2017, he publicly signalled his backing of the company on social media while promoting a new Hugging Face release.“Excited for the new release of #HuggingFace durant.ly/huggingface - proud investor!” Durant wrote.Nearly a decade later, that early bet has taken on a very different significance following Nvidia's agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion.Pompliano estimates that Durant and Kleiman's investment could now be worth more than $60 million, a figure that would turn the original $250,000 commitment into an extraordinary return.“He likely made more than $60 million in this investment alone,” Pompliano wrote, calling it “one of the best athlete investments ever.”The size of that potential return should nevertheless be treated carefully. Durant's exact ownership stake in Hugging Face has not been made public, so the $60 million figure is an estimate rather than a confirmed payout. The final amount he could receive will depend on the stake he actually holds and the terms and structure of Nvidia's acquisition.Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion, with the deal officially announced on September 3, 2026.According to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Hugging Face chief executive Clement Delangue, the AI company's team approached Nvidia during the summer as it looked to expand its computing resources.Hugging Face is expected to continue operating as an open platform for the global AI community following the acquisition.For Durant, the timing turns an early venture bet into a potentially extraordinary paper return. Pompliano's estimate would represent roughly a 23,900% return on the original $250,000 investment.It would also put the potential windfall above Durant's biggest single-season NBA salary.Durant is entering his 19th NBA season and is scheduled to earn $43.9 million with the Houston Rockets during the 2026-27 season, according to Spotrac.His contract is a two-year, $90 million deal, with a $46.1 million player option for 2027-28.Even after 18 NBA seasons, Durant has never earned $60 million in salary in a single season. His highest salary to date was $53.3 million last season, according to Spotrac.Across his NBA career, Durant has accumulated $501.1 million in earnings, according to Bleacher Report.That makes the estimated Hugging Face return unusual even by the standards of one of the NBA's highest-paid players: a reported investment of $250,000 could potentially produce more than he has ever earned from the NBA in one season.Durant has also spoken openly about the possibility of retirement, particularly after former teammate Russell Westbrook announced his own retirement.During an episode of, Durant said:“I'm on deck,” he said. “... It's a young man's game. Even though I still feel like I can play, I always hear, 'you're 38, you're 39. You're getting up there.' I get that. But I put everything into the game, and I'm cool with whatever happens moving forward. I'm going to continue putting everything into the game until I can't.”At 38, Durant's investment activity has therefore become an increasingly significant part of his business career away from basketball.The potential Hugging Face windfall is not Durant and Kleiman's only notable investment success.Through 35V and other investment vehicles, the pair have built a portfolio spanning technology, finance, consumer businesses, sports and other sectors.Among their investments are companies including Robinhood and Coinbase, both of which have since gone public.The portfolio also includes Acorns, Dapper Labs, Kalshi, Spindrift and Whoop, alongside stakes in the Philadelphia Union of Major League Soccer and Paris Saint-Germain.The Hugging Face investment nevertheless stands apart because of the size of the reported return relative to the original commitment.For now, the final number remains dependent on Durant's undisclosed stake and the completion and structure of Nvidia's acquisition. The $60 million-plus figure is Pompliano's estimate, not a confirmed payment to Durant.
Article Summary: Durant invested $250,000 in Hugging Face before its rise to prominence. Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition of the AI company changed the equation. The potential return is bigger than Durant's annual NBA salary. It would also put the potential windfall above Durant's biggest single-season salary.

Article Title: L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes $5.1 million hit on futuristic mansion after listing it for $32.5 million and making multiple price cuts
Article Text:
L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes major mansion loss. Image via: Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images | Realtor.com

Casey Wasserman sells futuristic mansion at a major loss

Inside the Bird Streets estate that inspired the loss

Did Casey Wasserman's controversy impact the sale?

Casey Wasserman had another financial hit involving his talent agency

Casey Wasserman closed the door on his futuristic Hollywood Hills home. The numbers, however, were not what he expected. The chairman of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics sold his award-winning Bird Streets estate for $18.5 million, a steep comedown from the $32.5 million he originally asked for it.The sale caps months of markdowns on a house once celebrated for its design. It also lands at an odd moment for the 52-year-old sports and entertainment mogul, whose name has been tied to headlines that have nothing to do with real estate.Casey Wasserman listed the property in September 2025, five years after it won the AIA Los Angeles Award for the city's most influential architecture. Buyers weren't rushing in. By February, he had shaved $2.6 million off the price, dropping it to $29.9 million. Still, it wasn't enough, so the number fell again, this time to $24.9 million.Realtor.com reports the home eventually sold for $18.5 million. Wasserman had paid $23.6 million for it back in August 2020, which puts his loss on the deal at roughly $5.1 million. It was a heavy hit.The house sits on what the listing calls the most prime cul-de-sac in Bird Streets, one of the most exclusive pockets of the Hollywood Hills. Designed by XTEN Architects, the place draws heavily from Stanley Kubrick's "2001: A Space Odyssey," right down to ceilings that reportedly cost more than $1 million to build.Five bedrooms and seven bathrooms fill roughly 12,000 square feet, and the primary suite leans into a dark, moody look with glass walls that pull in light and sweeping views. A wall installation inside reads "More, Faster, Now," while an eight-car underground garage sits below a home that also includes a private theater, a dance studio, and an infinity pool overlooking the hillside.It's a far cry from the last mansion Wasserman parted with. In June 2020, he sold his custom Beverly Hills estate, the Foothill Estate, to music executive David Geffen for $68 million. That home was built where his grandfather, the late entertainment titan Lew Wasserman, once lived, and it had originally been listed for $125 million.The sale comes months after Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass publicly called for Wasserman to step down as LA28 chairman. Her reasoning traced back to emails between Wasserman and Ghislaine Maxwell that surfaced in Department of Justice files released in February 2026. Bass didn't hold back when asked about it, telling CNN, "My opinion is that he should step down."Wasserman has said his contact with Maxwell and Jeffrey Epstein amounted to one humanitarian trip to Africa in 2002 and a handful of emails he now regrets. The LA28 board's executive committee reviewed the matter and sided with him, stating that his relationship with the pair "did not go beyond what has already been publicly documented." He kept his post.Whether the controversy nudged buyers away from the mansion is impossible to say for certain. But the timing, arriving in the same stretch as the price cuts, hasn't gone unnoticed.The house wasn't the only asset Wasserman put up for sale this year. Days after the LA28 committee finished its review, he told staff at his talent agency, Wasserman, that he had begun selling the company. In his memo, he wrote that he had become a distraction to its work and said Mike Watts would take over daily operations while he focused on the Olympics.The fallout from the Maxwell emails had already cost the agency clients. Chappell Roan, Odesza, Orville Peck, and retired soccer star Abby Wambach all cut ties. By July 2026, the agency was working toward a buyout of Wasserman's stake backed by Providence Equity Partners, with Watts stepping in as CEO and Providence taking majority ownership.
Article Summary: L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes major mansion loss. Wasserman had paid $23.6 million for it back in August 2020, which puts his loss on the deal at roughly $5.1 million. The sale comes months after Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass publicly called for Wasserman to step down as LA28 chairman.

Article Title: ‘Thank You, Colombia’: Captain James Rodríguez, 35, announces retirement from international football after extraordinary 15-year career
Article Text:
FILE - Colombia's James Rodriguez celebrates after defeating Costa Rica at the end of a friendly soccer match in Bogota, Colombia, Monday, June 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Fernando Vergara, File)

From a winning debut to Colombia's record cap holder

The captaincy, the tears and one more World Cup

Why James Rodríguez decided to walk away

35

Rodríguez's club career continues in Colombia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For 15 years, James Rodríguez was one of the first names that came to mind whenever Colombia walked onto a football pitch. The No. 10 shirt became closely associated with him, as did the captain’s armband, the spectacular goals and the expectations that followed him through three World Cups. On Tuesday, Rodríguez announced his international retirement in an emotional video, telling Colombian fans that it was time to close “one of the most important chapters” of his life. After 131 appearances for his country, the legendary No. 10 has brought that chapter to an end.Rodríguez's international story began in October 2011, when he made his Colombia debut against Bolivia and immediately announced himself by scoring the winning goal.He was only beginning what would become a 15-year relationship with the national team, eventually playing at the 2014, 2018 and 2026 World Cups. Colombia did not qualify for the 2022 tournament in Qatar, meaning Rodríguez's international career ultimately spanned three editions of football's biggest competition despite the four-year absence. He is tied with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincon for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian.The tournament that defined his reputation, however, came in Brazil in 2014.Rodríguez scored six goals in five matches to win the World Cup Golden Boot, including the extraordinary volley against Uruguay in the last 16 that became one of the defining goals of the tournament and later won the FIFA Puskás Award.Colombia reached the quarter-finals before losing to hosts Brazil, but Rodríguez's performances had already changed the trajectory of his career. After the tournament, he earned his move from Monaco to Real Madrid, where he would play alongside some of the biggest names in world football.For Colombia, meanwhile, the No. 10 had become much more than a shirt number.Rodríguez eventually took on the responsibility of captaining his country as well, carrying the armband during a period in which Colombia remained one of South America's strongest sides.He finished his international career as Colombia's record cap holder, level with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincón for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian, while his final figures stood at 131 appearances, 31 goals and 43 assists.Rodríguez's relationship with Colombia was never defined solely by the highlights.In his retirement message, he acknowledged the difficult periods alongside the celebrations and explained what representing the national team had meant to him throughout his career.“Today, I want to talk to you from the heart,” James said on social media on Tuesday. “After many years, many games and joys, and difficult moments, it's time to close one of the most important chapters in my life: my journey with the Colombian national team.”He described the responsibility attached to the shirt in equally personal terms.“Wearing this shirt was a dream, but also a huge responsibility,” James added. “Every time I entered a court, I understood that he didn't play just for me. I played for my family, teammates, thousands of Colombians who dreamed of all of us.“I had the honor of wearing the No. 10 shirt and also the captain's armband. I always tried to do it with respect, responsibility and understanding what it meant to represent Colombia. I had good days and very difficult ones, but I never stopped feeling proud of these colors.”His final appearance came on July 7, when Colombia faced Switzerland in the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup.The match finished 0-0 after extra time, before Switzerland won the penalty shootout 4-3, bringing Rodríguez's fourth and final World Cup campaign to an end.It also meant his last match for Colombia ended without the fairytale finish that might have suited the player who had given the country one of its most memorable individual World Cup performances.There had been another significant chapter two years earlier.Rodríguez captained Colombia to the 2024 Copa América final, where Argentina won 1-0 after extra time. It was Colombia's first appearance in the Copa América title match in 23 years, although Rodríguez ultimately finished his international career without a senior international trophy.His announcement was direct, with Rodríguez making clear that his decision was not about distancing himself from Colombia but about bringing an important period of his life to a natural conclusion.The caption accompanying his retirement video said: “Thank you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the greatest honours of my life.”He ended the message with the same sense of gratitude.“I'm leaving calmly because I gave everything. Thank you for every moment, thank you Colombia,” Rodríguez said.Rodríguez is now, and while his international career is finished, he has made clear that he is not finished with football.Just last week, Rodríguez joined Atlético Nacional on a contract running through next June after leaving Minnesota United.The move takes him back to Colombian football for the first time since his teenage years at Envigado, where his professional career began, and gives the veteran midfielder an opportunity to continue playing in his home country after closing the door on international football.Atlético Nacional becomes the 14th club of a career that has taken Rodríguez through some of the biggest teams in Europe and North America, including Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Everton.His club honours include two Champions League titles and two LaLiga crowns, while his international career produced the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup, 31 goals, 43 assists and more appearances for Colombia than any other player.There will be no more World Cup nights in the yellow shirt, no further Copa América campaigns and no additional occasions for Rodríguez to walk out wearing Colombia's No. 10 or captain's armband.For a generation of Colombian supporters, those two symbols had become inseparable from the same player.Now Rodríguez will try to write the final pages of his playing career at Atlético Nacional, while the Colombia team begins the task of imagining its midfield and its No. 10 shirt without the player who occupied both for so long.
Article Summary: James Rodríguez announced his retirement from international football on Tuesday. The No. 10 made 131 appearances for Colombia, including three World Cups. He is tied with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincon for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian. He won the World Cup Golden Boot in Brazil in 2014.

Article Title: Ex-Pakistan batter calls India 'arrogant' as he defends Mohsin Naqvi after Asia Cup trophy row

Former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf has come out in support of Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President and Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the trophy controversy following the Women's Asia Cup final.For the second successive year, an Indian team did not collect the Asia Cup trophy after winning the tournament. Harmanpreet Kaur 's side defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final to claim a record-extending eighth title, but the players stayed in the dressing room when the presentation ceremony began.The Indian team's decision came after it had made it clear that it would not accept the trophy from Naqvi, who is currently the ACC president as well as the PCB chairman.Naqvi had largely stayed away from the presentation area during the final, but was seen in the VIP box during the final over. The ceremony was subsequently delayed by around 45 to 50 minutes before eventually getting underway.Yousuf, however, defended Naqvi and accused India of displaying "arrogance" in a post on X on Tuesday.“When national pride turns into arrogance, victory brings no reward. A team may win, but a nation without humility remains a loser! No trophy, only heels on heads.#MohsinNaqvi,” Yousuf wrote on X (formerly Twitter).The latest incident mirrors what happened after last year's men's Asia Cup. India had refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi following the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor. The men's tournament was also marked by heightened tensions between India and Pakistan, with Naqvi accused of fuelling the situation through anti-India statements on social media.India's women's team maintained a similar stance this year. Head coach Amol Muzumdar later said the BCCI had decided against accepting the trophy from Naqvi and that the players simply followed the board's position.A day later, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said India's position had been communicated to Naqvi well before the final, but the ACC president still attended the presentation ceremony.Saikia and BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla were both present at the Women's T20 Asia Cup final.When the delayed presentation finally began, only Sri Lanka came out to collect their runners-up medals. Naqvi presented the runners-up cheque to Sri Lankan captain Chamari Athapaththu.After Athapaththu completed her broadcaster interview, the presentation proceedings came to an end, leaving India without the trophy despite their comprehensive victory in the final.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday. But the team did not accept the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi. Article Title: Aryna Sabalenka’s nightmare deepens as Elena Rybakina takes both US Open title and No. 1 ranking within 72 hours
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina (Getty Images)

Aryna Sabalenka loses world No. 1 ranking to Elena Rybakina

Elena Rybakina defeats Sabalenka in US Open final

Aryna Sabalenka’s US Open campaign ended with more than a painful final defeat. In just three days, the Belarusian lost the world No. 1 ranking and then watched her bid for a third straight US Open title disappear against Elena Rybakina. The collapse marked a rare low point in Sabalenka’s recent Grand Slam run, but her response afterward showed that she is already thinking about getting back to the top.The warning signs had been building before Sabalenka even reached the US Open final.Rybakina had entered the tournament with a genuine chance to overtake Sabalenka at No. 1. Her rise had gained momentum after she defeated Sabalenka in the WTA Finals Riyadh championship match at the end of 2025. She then produced another dramatic win over the Belarusian at the Australian Open, recovering from a 3-0 deficit in the deciding set.Sabalenka knew the ranking battle was becoming difficult to ignore. Yet she tried to keep her attention on the court.“I completely separate myself from that, because it’s just guessing. It’s like if, if, if, if. I’m just trying to bring my best tennis every time I’m competing out there and basically fight for it,” she said after reaching the quarter-finals.Rybakina ultimately made the ranking change unavoidable. She defeated Qinwen Zheng to reach the US Open semi-finals, officially ending Sabalenka’s 99-week run at No. 1.Sabalenka responded with a short but striking message.“I don’t care!”Her point was clear. A Grand Slam trophy mattered more to her than holding the top ranking.Unfortunately for Sabalenka, she would lose both.Rybakina entered the final after beating Coco Gauff in the semi-finals, while Sabalenka arrived as the defending champion and favourite. She also carried an impressive record at Arthur Ashe Stadium, having not lost there in two years.The stakes were enormous. A victory would have made Sabalenka only the third woman in tennis history to win the US Open three consecutive times.Rybakina had other plans.The Kazakh player took the opening set 6-4, using her powerful groundstrokes to overcome a difficult start on serve. Sabalenka fought back in the second, breaking late to take it 7-5 and force a deciding set.That comeback proved temporary.Rybakina regained control in the third set, breaking for a 2-1 advantage before adding another break at 5-2. She finished the match with her 12th ace, completing a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory in two hours and 21 minutes.The result gave Rybakina her first US Open title and strengthened her claim as the leading force in women's tennis. When the WTA publishes its updated rankings, she will become the 30th woman in the Open Era to reach No. 1.For Sabalenka, the defeat ended a remarkable run. She will finish 2026 without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.Still, she did not leave New York sounding defeated."I don't even know how many weeks I was able to be there, but it was amazing. Let's see if Elena can beat me in that. If she continues playing like that, I'm in trouble"Her words carried a warning as much as a compliment. Sabalenka may have lost her crown, but she already has her eyes on taking it back.
Article Summary: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in the US Open final. The Kazakh becomes the 30th woman in the Open Era to reach No. 1. The loss ends the Belarusian's 99-week run at the top of the rankings.

Article Title: Inspiring story on fatherhood: “Becoming a father has changed me; I want to set a good example” – how Alexander Zverev’s daughter inspired him to become a better man on and off the tennis court
Article Text:
Inspiring story on fatherhood: “Becoming a father has changed me; I want to set a good example” – how Alexander Zverev’s daughter inspired him to become a better man on and off the tennis court

What did Alexander Zverev mean when he said fatherhood changed him?

Why is setting a good example so important to Zverev?

Has fatherhood changed the way Zverev handles his emotions?

What kind of example does Zverev want to set for his daughter?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alexander Zverev has opened up about how becoming a father changed the way he sees himself, especially when it comes to his behavior on and off the tennis court. The German tennis star became a father to his daughter, Mayla, in 2021, and says the experience has given him a different sense of responsibility. Zverev has always been an emotional player, and his frustration has sometimes been visible during matches. But he now looks at those moments differently because he knows his daughter will one day see how he handled them. When Zverev said, “Becoming a father has changed me; I want to set a good example,” he was not simply talking about becoming calmer during tennis matches. He was talking about the kind of person he wants to be for his daughter and the values he hopes she will see in him as she grows up.Alexander Zverev’s comment was mainly about responsibility. Before becoming a father, his focus was largely on himself, his career and his results. Like any top athlete, he wanted to win, and losing could bring out strong emotions. He has had moments on the court when his frustration got the better of him, including angry outbursts and racket-smashing incidents.But becoming a father gave him something bigger to think about.Now, Zverev is not only thinking about what happens when he wins or loses a match. He is also thinking about the person his daughter will see when she looks at him. That can change the way someone reacts to difficult situations.His words suggest that he does not want Mayla to grow up seeing him as someone who lets anger control him. Instead, he wants her to see a father who can deal with pressure, disappointment and difficult moments without losing control.That does not mean Zverev suddenly stopped being emotional. Tennis is still an intense sport, and he remains a passionate competitor. The difference is that he has become more aware of how he handles those emotions.For him, fatherhood has added another reason to keep improving as a person.When Alexander Zverev talks about setting a good example, he is thinking about much more than tennis.Children often learn by watching their parents. They notice how their parents react when things go wrong, how they treat other people and how they handle pressure. Zverev appears to understand that his daughter will learn from what he does, even when he is not directly teaching her anything.That is why his own behavior matters to him.Zverev has spoken about wanting to be remembered not only for what he achieved on a tennis court but also for the person he was away from the sport. That is an important part of his comment about fatherhood.Winning major tournaments can define an athlete’s career, but Zverev knows that his daughter will not judge him only by the number of trophies he wins. For her, he is simply going to be her father.That gives his words a different meaning.He wants Mayla to be proud of him not just because he is a successful tennis player, but because he tries to be a good person. His work away from tennis also matters to him, including his efforts through the Alexander Zverev Foundation, which supports children living with Type 1 diabetes.So, setting a good example is about his whole life. It is about showing his daughter that success is not only about winning. It is also about how you treat people, how you deal with setbacks and what you do when nobody is keeping score.This is probably one of the clearest ways to understand his quote.Zverev has never hidden the fact that he can be emotional on the court. Tennis can be frustrating because players are often alone with their thoughts for several hours. One mistake can change a match, and the pressure is even greater when a major title is at stake.Earlier in his career, Zverev sometimes struggled to control that frustration. His emotions could become a major part of his matches.However, he has made an effort to change that side of himself.Zverev has pointed out that he had not smashed a racket for several years, showing that he has become better at controlling his anger. While that change cannot be credited only to fatherhood, becoming a parent has clearly given him another reason to work on himself.There is also a bigger lesson behind this.Being a role model does not mean being perfect. Zverev can still get frustrated. He can still have bad days. What matters is how he responds when things do not go his way.That is something he can eventually pass on to his daughter.He wants her to understand that losing is not the end of the world and that making mistakes is part of life. What matters is picking yourself up and trying again.In that sense, controlling his emotions is not only helping Zverev as a tennis player. It is also part of the person he wants to become as a father.At the heart of Zverev’s quote is a simple idea: he wants his daughter to see the best version of him.His career will continue to have wins and losses. There will be tournaments where everything goes right and others where nothing seems to work. But those results will eventually become part of the past.The example he sets for Mayla can last much longer.Zverev wants her to see someone who works hard for what he wants but also understands that life is bigger than tennis. He wants to show her how to deal with pressure without allowing it to change who you are.He also wants his actions away from the court to matter. His charity work, his relationship with his family and the way he carries himself are all part of the legacy he wants to build.For Zverev, fatherhood has therefore brought a new kind of motivation. He is still competing for titles and trying to reach the top of tennis, but there is now someone watching him who matters in a completely different way.That is what makes his statement about becoming a father so meaningful.“Becoming a father has changed me” is not simply about his life changing after Mayla was born. It is about realizing that his choices can influence someone else. And when he says, “I want to set a good example,” he is saying that he wants his daughter to grow up seeing a man who learns from his mistakes, controls his emotions, treats people well and keeps trying to become better.For Zverev, that may ultimately be one of the most important things he can leave behind.
Article Summary: Alexander Zverev has opened up about how becoming a father changed the way he sees himself. The German tennis star became a father to his daughter, Mayla, in 2021. He says the experience has given him a different sense of responsibility.

Suzy Kolber gave ESPN 27 years. She was there for the launch of ESPN2. She was the first name attached to the X Games. She helped carry Monday Night Football when it moved to the network. When the layoffs came in 2023, she saw it coming. What she did not see coming was the part that broke her: ESPN was not going to say a single word about her leaving.Why did Suzy Kolber's ESPN exit hurt more than just losing her job?ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro had already warned Kolber about a week before the cuts were announced. He told her directly, "Suzy, there's a whiteboard and your name's on it." She processed it. She braced herself. She sat at her kitchen table with her daughter and said, "I think this is really happening."None of that was easy. But it was manageable, in the way that people find a way to manage things they can see coming. What caught her off guard was what came next.She found out that ESPN planned to make no public statement about her departure. No acknowledgment, no thank-you, not even a brief mention of someone who had been one of the most visible people at the network for nearly three decades.That is when it really hit her."Probably the most emotional thing was Norby saying to me [ESPN was] not going to say anything. I was the first person hired for the launch of ESPN2. I was the first person assigned to the X Games. I was part of Monday Night Football's move to ESPN. I was part of some pretty big franchises," Kolber said during an appearance on Richard Deitsch's Sports Media podcast."I was like, 'You're not gonna say a word? Not thanks for 27 years. Just acknowledge it?'"So she took it into her own hands. She wrote her own announcement, reached out to Adam Schefter and longtime ESPN PR executive Chris LaPlaca to help amplify it, and posted it herself. The moment it went live, something inside her gave way."As soon as I saw [the post] go live, I had a good three to five minutes of full-on sobbing," she said. "It was real."What did Suzy Kolber say during her final call with ESPN's Norby Williamson?The call that officially ended her ESPN career came from former executive Norby Williamson. At some point in the conversation, Williamson reminded Kolber that speaking negatively about the network could have consequences.She did not take that quietly."I have been the ultimate good soldier. All the [expletive] I've seen, I have never said one negative thing about this company. Like, do you think I'm going to start now?" she pushed back.It is a line that says a lot about how Kolber carried herself through 27 years. She had seen plenty. She stayed quiet through all of it. And even in the room where they were letting her go, her first instinct was not anger toward ESPN.It was defense of her own record.That kind of loyalty, met with institutional silence on the way out, is what made this story land the way it did for people. It was not really about a firing. It was about what happens when an organization forgets that the people who built it were actually people.
Article Summary: Suzy Kolber worked for ESPN for 27 years. She was the first name attached to the X Games and Monday Night Football. Kolber was let go in 2023. ESPN planned to make no public statement about her departure. She wrote her own announcement and posted it online.

Article Title: Josh Jacobs battery case: Victim’s lawyers make major move to protect privacy as sealed evidence draws attention
Article Text:
Josh Jacobs battery case (Getty Images)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The legal chapter surrounding Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs took a significant turn Tuesday when attorneys representing the woman at the center of his battery case filed a motion to seal evidence. The move came days after Jacobs pleaded no contest last Thursday to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges, both tied to a May incident involving his then-girlfriend. With the criminal phase largely settled, the focus has now shifted from the courtroom to what the public may or may not get to see.Why are the victim's lawyers trying to seal evidence in the Josh Jacobs case?Attorneys Ramses Jalalpour and Amir Tahmassebi stated Tuesday that "the motion is consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy, particularly in light of Mr. Jacobs taking responsibility for his actions in the criminal proceeding."That framing matters. The lawyers are not contesting the outcome or disputing what happened. They are, specifically, drawing a line around how much of the surrounding documentation becomes public record. The motion targets a wide range of materials. The woman sought to seal police and supplemental reports, dispatch records, recordings, photographs, witness statements, investigative notes, forensic materials, medical or treatment-related information, and digital evidence.Her reasoning was stated plainly in the supporting brief. She wanted "only to prevent unnecessary public disclosure of information that identifies or locates her, reveals intimate details of the victimization or creates a material risk of further harm to her."One piece of evidence in particular has drawn attention: surveillance footage from the garage camera system, which police said corroborated the woman's account of what happened. That video has not been released. Given the motion now formally in place, it may never become public.What happens to Josh Jacobs now? His NFL future and pending suspensionJacobs, a three-time Pro Bowler, currently sits on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list, which keeps him away from playing and practicing while allowing him to continue receiving his paycheck. He can access team facilities for meetings, individual workouts, therapy, and rehabilitation.On the legal side, Jacobs was ordered to pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs following the no-contest plea. Under the agreement with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge could be dropped within a year, provided he stays out of trouble, avoids contact with the victim, completes counseling, submits to supervision, and pays restitution.The criminal case is functionally resolved. The NFL's response, however, is not. Jacobs could still face a league suspension, and with the exempt list status already in effect, Green Bay's offensive backfield has been operating without its starting running back before Week 1 of the new season has barely settled.The league has not publicly committed to a timeline, which leaves the Packers in an uncomfortable holding pattern. Whether the sealed evidence affects how the NFL conducts its own internal review remains to be seen. But the request itself signals that, for the woman involved, getting through this with some measure of privacy intact is the only thing that matters now.
Article Summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest last week to misdemeanor battery. The woman at the center of the case filed a motion to seal evidence Tuesday. The motion targets a wide range of materials, including police and supplemental reports. Jacobs could still face a league suspension.

Article Title: What did Adam Silver tell Sophie Cunningham? Fever guard reveals details of private call with NBA boss
Article Text:

Sophie Cunningham reveals conversation with Adam Silver

Why Cunningham wants a WNBA commissioner who unites the league

Sophie Cunningham picked up the phone recently and found NBA commissioner Adam Silver on the other end, wanting her honest read on what the WNBA needs in its next leader. The Indiana Fever guard confirmed the call took place, though she kept most of it close, choosing instead to speak in broad terms about the kind of person she thinks should take over from Cathy Engelbert.Talking with reporters after practice, Cunningham didn't hand Silver a shortlist of names. She laid out a vision instead, one built around unity and genuine access for players, a pointed nod to what many around the league feel has been missing during Engelbert's run at the top.Sophie Cunningham addressed the call on Monday, a few days after Engelbert announced she would step down at the end of 2026. Silver is expected to lead the search for her replacement, since the WNBA commissioner answers directly to him. Neither the league nor Cunningham confirmed exactly what was said between the two, but the fact that Silver reached out to a player at all says something about how much her voice carries these days.“I think the WNBA has always been a place for people to feel safe and comfortable. I think there’s all types of walks in this organization, or in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome. But I do think with that you need someone who’s going to unite everybody because it can be so different.But that doesn’t mean it’s a bad thing. I think it makes it a lot of fun,” Cunningham said.Cunningham, 30, has become one of the more talked-about figures in the league this year, largely because of her outspoken stance on transgender athletes competing in women's sports. That position has drawn protests at road games and turned her into a polarizing figure for some fans. Whatever friction it's created outside the arena, it clearly hasn't stopped Silver from valuing her input on league matters that go well beyond the court.She didn't put forward any specific candidates for the job, saying she trusts Silver and his team to make that call. What she did offer was a clear picture of the qualities she wants in whoever takes the role next.The 6-foot-1 guard was direct about what matters most to her. She wants someone capable of bringing together a locker room, and a league, that includes a wide range of personalities and perspectives. "You need someone who's going to unite everybody," Cunningham said, framing that difference as a strength rather than a problem.Engelbert has faced criticism for keeping her distance from players, and Cunningham shared that she wants the opposite from the next commissioner: someone willing to build real relationships with the athletes, even when that means delivering decisions players won't love. An open line of communication, she argued, changes how those tough calls land.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham says she spoke with NBA commissioner Adam Silver about the WNBA. The Indiana Fever guard says she wants a commissioner who unites the league. Silver is expected to lead the search for Cathy Engelbert's replacement. Engelbert announced she would step down at the end of 2026.

Article Title: Jos Buttler breaks Rohit Sharma's record, becomes second-highest T20I run-scorer

Buttler moves past Rohit

England dominate Sri Lanka

Jos Buttler has moved past Rohit Sharma to become the second-highest run-scorer in men's T20I cricket, adding another major milestone to his decorated international career.The England wicketkeeper-batter reached the landmark during the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday, where the hosts cruised to a 119-run victory and took a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.Buttler came into the game needing to close the gap on Rohit's tally of 4,231 runs. He did so in style, smashing 80 off 44 balls to take his overall T20I tally to 4,292 runs from 161 matches.His innings featured eight fours and three sixes, and Buttler brought up his half-century in only 29 deliveries. He then combined with England captain Harry Brook to put Sri Lanka under severe pressure.The pair added 128 runs for the second wicket, continuing a prolific partnership after their record 233-run stand against India in England's previous T20I.Buttler eventually fell for 80, but Brook carried on to produce the defining innings of the match, hammering an unbeaten 114 off 49 balls. England finished with 254/4 from their 20 overs.Buttler's latest knock took him to 4,292 T20I runs at an average of 34.33. His tally includes two centuries and 29 fifties.He has now moved ahead of Rohit, who finished his T20I career with 4,231 runs, and sits second on the all-time men's list.Pakistan's Babar Azam remains at the top with 4,596 runs from 145 matches at an average of 38.94.Sri Lanka's chase never gathered momentum after England's imposing total. They managed only six runs from the opening two overs before Sonny Baker began making an impact with his pace.Baker claimed 3/12 from four overs, while Jamie Overton and Liam Dawson took two wickets each as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 135 in 19 overs.Dunith Wellalage offered some resistance with a 33-run cameo, but England remained firmly in control throughout the chase.The victory also extended England's winning run against Sri Lanka in T20Is to 13 consecutive matches.Brook was named Player of the Match after his unbeaten 114, but the night also belonged to Buttler, who moved past Rohit to claim second place on the T20I run-scoring charts.
Article Summary: Jos Buttler becomes second-highest run-scorer in men's T20I cricket. England wicketkeeper-batter reaches landmark against Sri Lanka. England beat Sri Lanka by 119 runs to take 1-0 lead in three-match series.

Article Title: New Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson hit with personal tragedy as he misses introductory press conference
Article Text:
Mitchell Robinson misses Celtics debut after family tragedy. Image via: Elsa/Getty Images

Mitchell Robinson's brother was tragically hit by a car

Mitchell Robinson missed the Boston Celtics ' introductory press conference

Mitchell Robinson's first official introduction as a Boston Celtic did not go as planned. The new center missed Tuesday's introductory press conference after leaving Boston that morning to handle a personal family matter. While Paul George and Mike Conley met with the media, Robinson's situation remained private until more details emerged about a troubling incident involving his younger brother.Robinson later asked for prayers for his brother, Zeek, after he was reportedly hit by a car while jogging. The incident comes only months after Robinson dealt with another serious accident involving his sibling. For the 28-year-old center, a new chapter in Boston has now been overshadowed by a deeply personal family concern.Mitchell Robinson's younger brother Zeek was reportedly hit by a car while out for a jog, according to Celtics reporter Bobby Krivitsky. Robinson also shared a Facebook post asking people to pray for his brother.“Prayers for my little brother. my dawg can’t catch a break,” Robinson posted on Facebook.The latest incident is especially difficult because Robinson's family had already faced a serious car accident involving his younger brother earlier this year.Robinson previously revealed how shaken he was after learning about the crash. He was hundreds of miles away when he tried to contact his family and eventually saw his brother on FaceTime.“I began returning calls and texts, and when I FaceTimed my brother, I thought he was deceased,” Mitchell Robinson wrote. “He was wearing a neck brace, unresponsive, and not speaking. I broke down in tears, feeling like a failure for not being able to protect my siblings. Being 910 miles away, I felt helpless.“In a moment of frustration, I banged my hand on my truck…I would like to address the concerns regarding my finger, which was actually my knuckle.”Robinson fractured the fifth metacarpal in his right hand during the incident. He underwent surgery but returned to play during New York's championship run.Robinson was scheduled to join George and Conley at the Celtics' introductory press conference. Instead, he left Boston that morning to deal with the family matter.Celtics president Brad Stevens briefly explained Robinson's absence.“He unfortunately had to leave this morning…to attend to a personal matter.”The team later confirmed Robinson would be introduced at a later date.The absence came shortly after Robinson agreed to a three-year, $47.4 million contract with Boston following eight seasons with the Knicks. He had also been working out with his new teammates and expressing confidence about his upcoming season.“Was working out with my coach in Boston. You know what he said? He didn’t know that I had the s–t that I showed tonight,” Robinson said. “The ball handling, the shooting, the touch. Right now, I’m just so confident in myself. I don’t worry about what no one said.”He added that it was “going to be a great year for me.”For now, Robinson's focus is on his family.
Article Summary: Mitchell Robinson's younger brother Zeek was reportedly hit by a car while out for a jog, according to Celtics reporter Bobby Krivitsky. Robinson was scheduled to join Paul George and Mike Conley at the Celtics' introductory press conference. He left Boston that morning to deal with a personal matter.

Article Title: 'Athletes got an experience to stay in containers': Sharath Kamal on Asian Games accommodation challenge
Article Text:
India's Sharath Kamal Achanta (AP/PTI)

Athletes prepared for the challenge

At least one TT medal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s deputy chef-de-mission for the Asian Games, Achanta Sharath Kamal , believes Indian athletes will have little trouble adjusting to the unusual accommodation arrangements at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, despite concerns raised by some participating countries.India’s 501 athletes and 265 officials will stay in a mix of converted shipping containers, a docked cruise ship and hotels when the Games begin on September 19. While the container rooms have been criticised as cramped, Sharath said Indian athletes have already had some experience of staying in similar facilities."For the players, by the direction of the Sports Authority of India, we have had some containers built in various SAI campuses, where the athletes got an experience to stay in containers. And of course, cruise ships, we tried to replicate something like that," said Sharath, as quoted by news agency PTI.Around 4,000-5,000 athletes will stay on the luxury cruise liner Costa Serena at Nagoya Port, while around 2,000 will be housed in converted shipping containers at Garden Pier in Nagoya Bay. The rest will stay in hotels near competition venues in Aichi and, for some events such as swimming, in Tokyo.Sharath, who is also the vice chair of the Athletes Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), said the bigger concern was for officials, who did not get the same opportunity as athletes to experience the makeshift accommodation beforehand."But at the same time, players know what to expect. We have educated them very well. And I am pretty sure they will get accustomed quite quickly," he said."The important thing is the performance. I am sure they will be able to perform well."Sharath is also expecting India’s table tennis team to return with at least one medal. The 10-member squad includes five men and five women, with the men's doubles pair of Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah and the mixed doubles combination of Manush and Diya Chitale among India's medal hopes."My expectation is to win at least one medal, if not two. Last time, we got one medal in women's double. And prior to that, we got two bronze medals in 2018," Sharath said."The men's doubles pair of Manush and Manav, they are doing extremely well. They were world number two at one point in time. They are in the top four now. And they have a good chance of winning a medal," said the 44-year-old."So these two events, we have a good chance to win medals. And of course, team championships are always quite an open event."Table tennis competitions will be held from September 20 to 28.
Article Summary: India’s deputy chef-de-mission for the Asian Games, Achanta Sharath Kamal, believes Indian athletes will have little trouble adjusting to the unusual accommodation arrangements at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Around 4,000-5,000 athletes will stay on the luxury cruise liner Costa Serena at Nagoya Port, while around 2,000 will be housed in converted shipping containers.

Article Title: 'Don't make changes': Yuvraj Singh's warning to Gautam Gambhir and management ahead of 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
ROHIT SHARMA, VIRAT KOHLI

Yuvraj Singh warns against last-minute changes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup have already brought one major question into focus: what will their squad look like when the tournament gets underway in October?The World Cup will be staged in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, with India aiming to win the title for the third time after falling short in the 2023 final. With Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli having retired from the other formats of international cricket, their availability for the 50-over showpiece remains a key talking point.Amid the uncertainty, India's 2011 World Cup hero Yuvraj Singh has stressed the importance of one thing above all else: consistency.Speaking to Cricinfo, Yuvraj said India should settle on a core group of 16 to 20 players and give them regular opportunities in the limited number of ODIs available before the World Cup."They need to focus on building the same team to play in a year's time, because you don't want to make big changes at the last moment," Yuvraj Singh said.The former all-rounder believes regular game time will be particularly important with the ODI calendar becoming increasingly limited compared to T20 cricket."Whoever your players are, whether they are 16 or 20, it's important that everybody gets game time because obviously now there are more T20S and less 50-over cricket. Whatever matches there are, it's important that players get enough game time to prepare for the World Cup," he added.Yuvraj pointed to India's past struggles at major tournaments and argued that sudden changes close to a World Cup can disrupt a team's preparations."Every time India has faltered is when they've made some massive changes at the last moment or in the tournament. So I think it's important that we stick to a team that we believe can lift the 2027 World Cup and stick by those guys whether they fail or succeed till that moment.Belief in the squad is very important," Yuvraj further said.He also cited India's success in the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups as an example of how developing a settled group can help a team prepare for a major tournament. India also reached the 50-over World Cup final in 2023."That's something that we have also done in the last two T20 World Cups," Yuvraj said. "We also played the 50-over World Cup final [in 2023]. So we have had a lot of consistency in white-ball cricket. And that's what they need to do as well, to think of first qualifying for the semis and then going on to play in the last two [knockout matches]. I think that's a long way ahead. Focus should be on getting a squad ready, which is together and ready to fight in any situation," the star former all-rounder further went on to say.
Article Summary: India preparing for 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have retired from other formats of international cricket. Yuvraj Singh says India should settle on a core group of 16 to 20 players.

Article Title: “It’s a shame”: Why did Michael Page feel disrespected at the end of his UFC journey despite a 5-1 record?
Article Text:
Michael Page opens up on his UFC exit and the struggle behind it (Image via IG/X)

Michael Page believed his UFC record deserved a proper conversation

The deeper part of Michael Page’s story goes beyond his UFC record

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael “Venom” Page’s UFC journey was supposed to be about proving that his unique style could work at the highest level of MMA. He arrived in the promotion with a reputation built on speed, creativity and spectacular finishes. By the time his UFC run ended, however, the conversation had changed. Page had won five of six fights, yet he felt the way his departure was handled did not match what he had achieved. His disappointment was not simply about losing a contract. It was about communication, respect and the feeling that he never got the chance to understand where he stood. Now, Page is reflecting on a chapter that taught him as much about himself as fighting.Page joined the UFC in 2024 after becoming one of Bellator’s most recognizable fighters. His first appearance against Kevin Holland at UFC 299 gave fans an early look at what he could bring to the promotion.He won that fight by unanimous decision, using his movement and striking to frustrate Holland. While the spectacular finishes that had become part of Page’s identity did not arrive consistently afterward, the British veteran continued finding ways to win.His UFC record eventually reached 5-1. Four of those victories came consecutively, with his final win coming against Nursulton Ruziboev in Paris. From Page’s perspective, that record should have at least opened the door for another discussion with the promotion."I had goals to achieve, so regardless of anything, I was winning my fights, which says to me you get to stay," Page told Uncrowned. "That's the premise of this game. Success should breed more opportunities. So, I still felt like we'd sit down at the table.""What is the harm in allowing me to speak [after the fight]?" Page said. "I've seen fights that have been absolutely terrible, and they still get to go on the mic and say their piece. This is the second time it's happened to me."The way he eventually found out about his UFC future made the experience harder. Dana White later confirmed publicly that the promotion would not re-sign Page. Page was on vacation when he saw messages from people reacting to the news."I was just chilling on holiday, and I see I'm getting messages from people seeing the clip. OK, I guess that's where we're at," Page said.For Page, the bigger issue was not necessarily the decision itself. He said he would have accepted a difficult conversation if it had been handled directly."I'm always happy to have a conversation, regardless of if it's a difficult one or easy one. ... If you're not happy with the performances, have a conversation with me. ... At least it gives me a goal and something to work toward, and I know exactly where I stand with the partnership."Page’s UFC experience also forced him to examine something more personal. Despite continuing to win, he felt he was not producing the performances he knew he was capable of delivering."I just know what I'm capable of, and for some reason, I don't know what it is, I just feel like I'm not pushing myself enough in the fights," Page said. "It's weird to say, because I'm winning fights and I'm not at my best. It's just a shame that I haven't been able to really showcase my best, and yet I'm still beating fighters that are at the top of their game.""I realized it second fight in, that I was carrying a weight, and I shouldn't be. It was a case of figuring out how to not do that when I'm heading into these fights. How to not fixate on performing the way that I used to and just enjoy the performance.""It's a show. I'm excited about the things I can do with my walkout, this and that. I can visualize exactly how amazing and epic that's going to be. There's nobody I'm saying no to right now," Page said.At 39, Page still wants to compete. More importantly, he appears determined to leave the frustration of his UFC exit behind and rediscover the enjoyment that made him fall in love with fighting in the first place.
Article Summary: Michael "Venom" Page left the UFC after winning five of six fights. The 39-year- old felt the way his departure was handled did not match what he had achieved. Page said he would have accepted a difficult conversation if it had been handled directly.

Article Title: Shohei Ohtani and Mamiko Tanaka’s impactful journey outside the spotlight: How their family foundation is building a lasting legacy in baseball and beyond
Article Text:
Shohei Ohtani with his wife Mamiko Tanaka (Image via WireImage )

Shohei Ohtani and Mamiko Tanaka’s family foundation supports children, youth activity and animals in need

For Ohtani, the foundation is not the beginning of his charitable work. Instead, it brings together causes he has already supported over the years.
