Shohei Ohtani has spent much of his career under the brightest lights in baseball. From his historic two-way performances to his success with the Los Angeles Dodgers, his name has become closely linked with greatness on the field. Yet there is another side of Ohtani that has steadily gained attention. Alongside his wife, Mamiko Tanaka, he has taken steps to make giving back part of his family’s story.The launch of the Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation created a new platform for that work. Its focus on children and animals offers a different view of the MLB superstar, one centered on community, compassion and a legacy that can last well beyond his playing career.The Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation was established with two clear areas of focus. It aims to support initiatives that encourage children to stay active and live healthier lives while also helping organizations that rescue, protect and care for animals.The foundation’s mission statement says, “Our mission is to create healthier, happier communities by funding initiatives that inspire children to stay active and live well, and by supporting programs that rescue, protect, and care for animals in need.”The organization also carries a strong family connection. Its logo features figures representing Ohtani, Mamiko Tanaka, their daughter and their dog Decoy, also known as Dekopin. That detail gives the foundation a personal touch and connects its charitable goals with the family’s own interests.Animal welfare has been particularly visible in his recent efforts. After devastating wildfires struck Southern California in January 2025, Ohtani announced a $500,000 donation to help firefighters, people forced to evacuate and animals that needed assistance.His connection with animals has also reached children’s literature. Ohtani co-authored Decoy Saves Opening Day, a book inspired by his beloved dog. He said proceeds from the book would be donated to nonprofit animal rescue organizations, giving the project a purpose beyond entertainment.From 60,000 baseball gloves in Japan to disaster relief, Ohtani’s charitable work has grown with his global successOhtani’s support for children has also taken a very direct form. In 2024, he donated 60,000 baseball gloves to elementary schools across Japan. The gesture helped provide young players with equipment while connecting Ohtani’s own baseball journey with the next generation.The donation was significant because Ohtani’s rise began in Japan before he became one of Major League Baseball’s biggest stars. His success gave him a global platform, and his charitable efforts show how he has chosen to use that platform.His support has not been limited to youth baseball. The $500,000 contribution following the Southern California wildfires showed another side of his philanthropy, with his donation aimed at helping firefighters, displaced residents and animals affected by the disaster.The response from fans and supporters has also reflected interest in this quieter side of Ohtani’s life. His donations to disaster relief, support for young athletes and concern for animals have helped shape an image that goes beyond statistics and awards.The Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation now gives those efforts a long-term home. With Mamiko Tanaka and their family represented in its identity, the foundation carries a personal meaning as well as a charitable mission.Ohtani’s baseball career will ultimately be remembered through records, championships and MVP awards. But his decision to invest in children, animals and communities could give his legacy another lasting chapter. For a star accustomed to making history on the field, his family foundation offers a chance to make an impact in a very different way.
Article Summary: Shohei Ohtani and Mamiko Tanaka’s family foundation supports children, youth activity and animals in need. The foundation aims to support initiatives that encourage children to stay active and live healthier lives. It also helps organizations that rescue, protect and care for animals.

Article Title: IOA announces Randhir Singh, Jaspal Rana memorial trophies for best Asian Games athletes
Article Text:
Randhir Singh and Jaspal Rana (Image credit: Agencies)

Awards to honour Asian Games stars

Usha says no accommodation issues so far

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'We are Team India'

NEW DELHI: Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha on Tuesday announced two memorial awards named after veteran sports administrator late Randhir Singh and shooting great Jaspal Rana.The awards will be given to the best male and female athletes at the Asian Games Singh served as the IOA secretary general for 25 years from 1987 to 2012. He also served as the president of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). Singh died at the age of 79 in May this year.Rana, a multiple Asian and Commonwealth Games medallist and renowned pistol coach, died at the age of 49 in June. He was the coach of double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker.Usha made the announcement during the launch of a book on Rana titled "Maverick Jaspal", co-authored by senior sports journalists S Kannan and G Rajaraman."From this year, the IOA has decided to introduce two memorial trophies in the names of legendary Raja Randhir Singh and shooting great Jaspal Rana for the best athletes in the Asian Games," she said."The Raja Randhir Singh Trophy will be awarded to the best male athlete of the Asian Games, while the Jaspal Rana Trophy will be awarded to the best female athlete of the Asian Games to honour their contribution to Indian sports."Usha also said there were no accommodation-related issues for the Indian contingent at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, which is hosting the Asian Games.She said Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav would handle any problems if they arise."They (organisers) have to give rooms because they are the organisers. From our side, we will do our best, and there is a Chef de Mission, and if there are any problems, he will solve them," said Usha, who will leave for Japan on Wednesday.Asked about accommodation-related problems for the Indian cricket teams, Usha said: "I didn't get any complaints from there. They are all athletes, and we are Team India."Usha does not want to put pressure on athletesThe IOA chief also said she did not want to put any pressure on the athletes competing at the Asian Games."I don't want to give any pressure to our athletes. I think they have all gone there with confidence. Hope that they will do their best. The Indian government, sports ministry, and IOA have already provided them with whatever they wanted."
Article Summary: The awards will be given to the best male and female athletes at the Asian Games. Singh served as the IOA secretary general for 25 years from 1987 to 2012. Rana, a multiple Asian and Commonwealth Games medallist and renowned pistol coach, died at the age of 49 in June.

Article Title: Kolkata Metro authorities caution content creators against phone-sticking and running stunt
Article Text:
Kolkata Metro authorities are cautioning commuters against dangerous phone-sticking stunts.

Metro officials urge commuters not to treat trains and platforms as film sets.





KOLKATA: A reel that appears to show a passenger casually leaving his phone stuck to a moving Metro window before running in the direction of the moving train with a popular tune playing in the background is now making its way into Kolkata’s social-media ecosystem, prompting Metro authorities to caution commuters against attempting the stunt.The trend, which recently prompted a warning from Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), has been replicated on the Metro systems in several Indian cities. In Kolkata, too, similar “phone-sticking and running” videos are being noticed on social media, with officials warning that such attempts could put the creator and fellow commuters at risk, besides damaging the phone and causing inconvenience on platforms and inside coaches.“We urge commuters not to treat Metro trains and platforms as a film set. The concern is not only the phone: someone running along a departing train could collide with another commuter, lose balance or create a dangerous situation near the platform edge. We have asked RPF officials and station staff to be cautious about such attempts and are also appealing to passengers to discourage anyone attempting such stunt,” said a Metro spokesperson.The craze exploded nationally after Delhi-based influencer Nikhil Kochar posted a reel on the Delhi Metro’s Yellow Line. Grooving to the tune of ‘Manma Emotion Jaage’ from ‘Dilwale’, the video showed Kochar dancing on the platform before appearing to stick his phone to the train and run after it as it departed. The reel crossed 135 million views in two days and spawned a stream of imitations.But the apparent stunt is largely an illusion. There is no reliable evidence that Kochar’s phone remained attached to the moving train throughout the sequence. Viewers spotted reflections and differences in image quality and concluded that the final footage was shot from inside the coach and edited with the platform sequence. In the format being copied, the creators across the country have started to pose beside the train while a separate camera records from inside, creating the impression that the phone stuck to the window is filming the entire sequence.The trend has since travelled beyond Delhi. Similar “phone-sticking and running” videos have surfaced in Bengaluru.The practice has also been replicated with local trains, buses and even auto-rickshaws.Regular commuters echoed the concern, saying a few seconds of viral footage was not worth creating a risk for others. “These days people shoot reels and videos at public places without the consent of other passengers often creating disturbance for them. What looks like a clever camera trick online can become dangerous when people try to copy it for real and can create a bigger trouble for fellow commuters,” said Puja Sengupta, a regular commuter.
Article Summary: Kolkata Metro authorities are cautioning commuters against dangerous phone- sticking stunts. The trend, which recently prompted a warning from Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, has been replicated on the Metro systems in several Indian cities. The reel crossed 135 million views in two days and spawned a stream of imitations.

Article Title: 'I wish I was monster': 48 hours after cryptic Instagram post, woman cop found dead
Article Text:
A 28-year-old woman constable was discovered hanging in her Gandhinagar rented home.





AHMEDABAD: A decomposing body of 28-year-old woman constable posted at Shahibaug police headquarters was found hanging at her rented home in Sector 3D of Gandhinagar on Monday night, nearly 48 hours after she posted a cryptic message on Instagram.The deceased, Jhanvi Dabhi, originally from Ahmedabad, had been serving in the police force for five years. She was a divorcee and had been living alone in Gandhinagar.Police suspect Dabhi died around one-and-a-half to two days before her body was discovered. Her landlord alerted police late Monday after noticing a foul smell coming from her room. Sector 7 police reached the house and found her body hanging from a ceiling fan with a dupatta. The body was sent for postmortem and an accidental death report was registered.Two days before her death, Dabhi had uploaded a photograph of herself on Instagram with the message, “I wish I was monster you think I am “. Police are examining her social media activity and mobile phone to determine whether the post was linked to circumstances preceding her death.No suicide note was recovered from her house. Police have seized her phone and are examining her calls, messages and other digital evidence.Investigators are also collecting details about her colleagues and friends from Shahibaug headquarters.Dabhi had a difficult family history. Her mother had remarried after her father’s death. Her brother and sister lived with their paternal aunt in Shamlaji, police said.Dabhi had initially entered into a love marriage. After her husband’s death, she married his elder brother following family and social arrangements. The relationship later developed differences, and the couple divorced around one-and-a-half years ago.Relatives described Dabhi as an independent woman living on her own terms. They said she also enjoyed making Instagram reels. Police are examining whether she faced any personal or financial pressures.Forensic Science Laboratory assistance was being taken to establish the approximate time of death. Family members will also be questioned after the last rites.
Article Summary: Jhanvi Dabhi, originally from Ahmedabad, had been serving in the police force for five years. She was a divorcee and had been living alone in Gandhinagar. Her landlord alerted police late Monday after noticing a foul smell coming from her room. No suicide note was recovered from her house.

Article Title: ‘I was too scared to stop’: Gurgaon biker recounts chase and crash on GCR
Article Text:
Shivani (27) said the ordeal began when the car came dangerously close to her motorcycle. The car first swept past her at high speed.





GURGAON: “I was very scared, so I did not stop.”Two days after a Maruti Ciaz chased and hit her on Golf Course Road, throwing her off her Aprilia and into the path of speeding traffic, Shivani Chauhan told TOI she never wanted a confrontation — she only wanted to get away.Shivani (27) said the ordeal began when the car came dangerously close to her motorcycle. The car first swept past her at high speed. “I thought, maybe, he had not seen me or was in a hurry. But if you have gone that fast, then go straight ahead. What sense does it make to stop ahead, gesture at me, then hit me from behind and run away?” she asked.Shivani said the car’s occupants repeatedly asked her to stop. “There were four boys in the vehicle. They were, perhaps, drunk and kept chasing me. They wanted to say something, but I did not want to talk,” she added.Shivani said she slowed to around 50-60kmph as the car moved across her path. She estimated it was travelling at around 100kmph or more when it came alongside and struck her. She was flung onto the road as her motorcycle skidded away, sparks flying from the friction.She suffered bruises and injuries to her knee and hand, but said the protective gear prevented fractures or worse.“I thank God that I had my riding shoes and gloves. The way my hand hit the road made me realise what could have happened. I could have broken my shoulder or legs.”The incident was captured on the camera mounted on her bike. Another camera also recorded the car moving across lanes before the collision.But one question still haunts her. What if the timing had been slightly different? “What if there had been a difference of two or three seconds? I could have suffered much deeper injuries, my bones could have broken, or I could have died on the spot,” she said.The Ciaz sped away after the crash. One of Shivani’s friends chased it and caught up with it at a traffic signal, but Shivani said the driver denied responsibility and left again. The accused, Kalyan Bainsla (33), later gave a media interview, claiming a group of bikers had been riding aggressively and that Shivani suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn. He denied hitting her deliberately.Shivani rejected the version. “If you felt so bad for me, why did you not stop at that time?” she asked, questioning why nobody checked on her after the collision.Police subsequently arrested Bainsla in Rajasthan along with his cousin Lovneesh (32), who was also in the car. DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said police added Section 109 of BNS, for attempt to murder, after analysing the footage and added that the collision appeared deliberate. Sections 78 and 79, relating to stalking and insulting a woman’s modesty, were also added after Shivani’s statement.For Shivani, the incident is about more than one dangerous ride. “Every woman rider should be able to feel safe on the city’s roads. Unfortunately, that sense of security is still missing,” she said.Sunday was meant to be a simple escape from her routine of helping residents in Kalkaji with civic problems. Her father Roshan Chauhan, an AAP functionary, said she had bought her first motorcycle only five to six months ago. “Her Sunday routine was simple. She wanted to ride out, have tea and return home,” he added.Shivani had gone out with a group of bikers on Sept 13. The family learnt about the crash only the next day, when journalists reached their home.Shivani, a fashion designing graduate, contested the 2022 MCD election on an AAP ticket at 23 and finished second. She later continued working on civic issues in Kalkaji.
Article Summary: Shivani (27) said the ordeal began when the car came dangerously close to her motorcycle. The car first swept past her at high speed. She estimated it was travelling at around 100kmph or more when it came alongside and struck her. She was flung onto the road as her motorcycle skidded away.

Article Title: After Satya Niketan collapse, cops take ‘What worries you most?’ to Delhi’s PG hubs
Article Text:
Karol Bagh SHO talks to students living in PGs or rented accommodations





New Delhi: At 4pm, there was little reason for the police personnel waiting in Karol Bagh to expect a crowd. They had picked a spot surrounded by coaching centres and paying guest accommodations, knowing students would return from classes later in the evening. For now, the road carried its usual traffic, but the students they wanted to speak to were still scattered across the neighbourhood.The wait was part of a new Delhi Police approach to reach out to students living in PGs and rented accommodation, particularly in coaching hubs. The move has gained urgency after the Satya Niketan building collapse, which heightened concerns about their safety.By 5pm, the students began trickling in. One was stopped. Then another. A few stayed back as more joined them. Soon, a small group had gathered around Karol Bagh SHO Karuna Sagar.The first thing the SHO did was share his phone number. Students were told they could contact him directly if they faced a problem or noticed something requiring police attention.Then came the questions. How was the PG? Was there anything around the building that worried them? Did they feel safe walking through the neighbourhood?The answers quickly showed that safety extended far beyond the four walls of their accommodation.It wasn’t just about fire extinguishers, emergency exits or the building’s condition; it was also about what hung overhead, what collected on the road after rain, and what happened on the street outside.Kiran, a UPSC aspirant who has lived in the area for two years, said the recent rains had made him wary of exposed electrical wires and waterlogging. “If these wires fall into the water, there is fear of electrocution. It’s not just about how safe the building is. The overall area should be safe for students,” he said.In 2024, a UPSC aspirant had died of electrocution in west Delhi’s Patel Nagar, highlighting the risks posed by exposed electrical infrastructure during the monsoon.Another student, Abhinav, echoed similar concerns. “The wires are right above our heads. It is pathetic,” he said.Then there were worries beyond electricity. Aejaz, another student, recalled a theft in his lane a few days earlier. Others spoke about rash driving on roads used heavily by students. Some were also worried whether the lane outside was safe, the infrastructure maintained and the journey to their coaching centre free of avoidable risks.With electrical wiring emerging as a major concern, SHO Sagar said the next meeting would involve BSES officials. Issues falling under other agencies are being taken up with the departments concerned, officials said.For the students gathered around the SHO, the exercise offered something significant: they now had a number to call before a concern became a complaint, or a complaint became an emergency.The Karol Bagh interaction was not a one-off exercise. DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said teams from police stations across the city were reaching out to students, PG residents and coaching hubs to understand their concerns. Where an issue belongs to another agency, police are taking it up with the department concerned.
Article Summary: New Delhi Police approach to reach out to students living in PGs and rented accommodation, particularly in coaching hubs. Move gained urgency after Satya Niketan building collapse, which heightened concerns about their safety. Students were told they could contact him directly if they faced a problem or noticed something requiring police attention.

Article Title: ‘Ignored at first, only males in car’: Gurgaon biker says driver repeatedly came close before crash
Article Text:
In a fresh video statement, Sia said she had not initially noticed the car following her.

‘I was shaking and couldn’t ride’

(With inputs from ANI)





GURGAON: Woman biker Sia said she initially tried to ignore the car that later crashed into her on Golf Course Road, but became scared after the driver repeatedly came close to her bike and gestured for her to stop.In a fresh video statement, Sia said she had not initially noticed the car following her. She said the first indication that something was wrong came when it sped past her very closely, startling her.“I tried to ignore it at first. Then, the car slowed down and dropped back behind me,” she said.Sia claimed the car later pulled up alongside her, with the driver making gestures and trying to get her to stop. She said another man sitting next to the driver was also making gestures.“That’s when I got scared. You could clearly tell from his face that they had been drinking,” she said, adding that she could not see exactly how many people were inside because of the car’s tinted windows.Sia said she believed there were two more men in the back and added that, from what she could see, there were no women in the car.She said she signalled the driver to stay to the side and not come too close. When she sensed the vehicle veering towards her bike or trying to overtake, she accelerated slightly because she feared the driver might do something reckless.Meanwhile, a fellow rider tried to pull alongside her, she said, while another vehicle came between them, forcing her to slow down.Sia said her front-facing camera captured the car, which she claimed moved from the first lane to the third lane before hitting her. She said she fell from the bike and was left disoriented after the collision.She said another rider tried to stop the driver, but he insisted that the crash was not his fault and blamed her instead. According to Sia, the driver then jumped a red light, took a left turn and fled.Sia said the crash left both the front and rear brakes of her motorcycle broken, making it difficult to ride.The other riders helped her reach a biker’s cafe in Gurgaon, where she had been headed. One rider gave her a pillion seat, she said, while another later rode her damaged motorcycle.“I stayed for about an hour because I was absolutely terrified. I was literally shaking and couldn't ride my bike at all,” she said.Sia said she eventually rode another rider’s motorcycle before switching back to her own and taking it home.She also said a fellow biker who knew her from previous group rides had his camera running during the incident and recorded what happened.The crash video went viral on Monday. Accused driver Kalyan Baisla has denied deliberately hitting Sia and claimed that a group of bikers was riding aggressively, repeatedly overtaking and slowing down in front of his car.He said Sia suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn and that he had little time to react.Baisla has also denied fleeing the scene and claimed that the videos circulating online were edited by joining separate clips.
Article Summary: In a fresh video statement, Sia said she had not initially noticed the car following her. She said the first indication that something was wrong came when it sped past her. Accused driver Kalyan Baisla has denied deliberately hitting Sia and claimed that a group of bikers was riding aggressively.

Article Title: HBO CEO on Apple TV, which has been called 'the new HBO' by some, winning the most number of Emmy awards; and beating Netflix and Amazon
Article Text:
HBO at Emmys over the years

Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The iPhone-makers' Apple TV proved to be the most successful studio at the Emmys 2026. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total, including six “Pluribus” wins, three for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles,” three for “Palm Royale,” one for “Slow Horses” and one for “Mr. Scorsese.” This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.Interestingly, Apple TV has long been compared to HBO. In fact, Apple has even been called "the new HBO" at times by some analysts. HBO boss Casey Bloys was asked by Deadline after the awards show for his reaction to Apple’s performance. In an interview conducted during HBO Max’s afterparty at the San Vicente Bungalows, Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, spoke about the company’s Emmy win. Bloys was asked what he thinks about Apple TV’s performance and their first time finishing as the No. 1 platform at the Emmys?' To this, HBO CEO replied, "Well, I’m very happy because I think that they’re very handsome competitors, Zack and Jamie. Look, we’ve had very formidable competitors in going back to Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon, so [when] Apple, everybody, keeps us on our toes, I think we do our best work.It’s a little scary that they’re a trillion-dollar company, but we’ll continue to do what we do, which is put out the best shows that we can."Reacting to the wins, former Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote on Twitter, "Stories have the power to move us, inspire us, and bring us closer together. Congrats to the Apple TV creators, cast, and crews behind the incredible work celebrated at the Emmys for Widow’s Bay, Pluribus, Slow Horses, Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Palm Royale, and Mr. Scorsese!"HBO was first allowed entry into the Emmys in the year 1988. The studio has been a dominant force at the Emmys ever since, initially competing with the broadcast networks, then basic and premium cable networks and, most recently, streamers like Netflix, Apple TV and Amazon’s Prime Video.In 2026, HBO shared the No. 1 title with Netflix for most Emmy wins. This year, it finished second to Apple TV with 21 wins versus Apple's 28. HBO won Outstanding Drama Series for 'The Pitt' and Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series with DTF St. Louis. After HBO Max, at the No. 3 was Netflix. The American streaming giant got 16 wins. Netflix winners include “Beef,” “Love on the Spectrum,” “Bridgerton,” “The Beast in Me” and more.
Article Summary: Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total. This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.

Article Title: Scientists discovered an unnamed female mummy in 1935, the Egyptian Mummy has been left screaming for 3,000 years
Article Text:
Egyptian Mummy (Representative image)

3,000-year-old Egyptian mummy discovered in Thebes

Expensive materials used in the mummy's burial

Why was the ancient Egyptian mummy left screaming

Scientists examine the 'screaming woman' mummy

An ancient Egyptian mummy discovered in Thebes in 1935 has left scientists trying to explain one unusual detail for decades: her face appears frozen in a scream. The woman was buried about 3,000 years ago and had received an expensive burial treatment, making it unlikely that her strange expression was simply the result of poor mummification. As stated in reports, researchers examined the mummy again in 2024 using X-rays, CT scans and several laboratory techniques. They found no clear cause of death, but suggested that a severe and sudden event may have caused a phenomenon known as a cadaveric spasm, leaving the woman’s mouth open and her face contorted at the time of death.The unnamed woman was discovered in 1935 in Thebes, an ancient Egyptian city. Her coffin carried no inscription identifying her. Her appearance immediately drew attention because her mouth was open and her face looked as though she had died while screaming.At first, researchers considered whether poor embalming could have caused the expression. Ancient Egyptian embalmers normally took extensive steps to preserve a body and make it look as natural as possible.However, evidence from the woman’s burial suggested that her body had received careful and costly treatment.The mummy wore an elaborate wig made from date palm fibres. It had been dyed with reddish henna and covered with a crystalline powder containing quartz, magnetite and albite. Her body, clothing and wig were also treated with imported resins. One of the materials used was frankincense associated with Punt, a region known for exporting valuable goods including aromatic resins and gold. Juniper resin was also used.These details suggested that the woman came from a wealthy section of ancient Egyptian society and that her embalmers had not simply carried out a careless or incomplete mummification.One unusual detail remains difficult to explain: the woman’s internal organs were still inside her body. In many ancient Egyptian burials, organs were removed during the mummification process and preserved separately in canopic jars. However, the researchers noted that later embalming practices could sometimes involve drying the organs and returning them to the body. There was no visible incision showing that the organs had been removed.Her arms also provide a clue about her status. They were positioned at her sides and only partly met over her lap. The researchers said this suggests she was not a member of the royal family, as royal mummies were buried with their arms crossed over their chests.In 2024, mummy radiologist Sahar Saleem of Cairo University and Samia El-Merghani of Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities examined the mummy using several non-destructive methods. The investigation included X-rays and CT scans, as well as scanning electron microscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analysis.The researchers found that the woman was around 5 feet tall and died at about 48 years old. Signs of wear were visible in her teeth and joints. But the tests did not reveal a clear cause of death.The researchers suggested that the woman's unusual facial position may have been caused by a cadaveric spasm. This phenomenon can involve certain muscles becoming fixed at the moment of death, particularly in cases involving severe pain or panic. It is different from normal rigor mortis because it can affect specific muscles rather than the entire body.The researchers said the expression could indicate that the woman died in extreme pain.
Article Summary: Researchers examined the mummy again in 2024 using X-rays, CT scans and several laboratory techniques. They found no clear cause of death, but suggested that a severe and sudden event may have caused a cadaveric spasm. The researchers said the expression could indicate that the woman died in extreme pain.
